studyDetails.title: Exploring injury profiles in professional football: evidence from a five-year study and the role of the functional movement screen
studyDetails.journal: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation

studyDetails.sourceQuote: Exploring injury profiles in professional football: evidence from a five-year study and the role of the functional movement screen; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13102-025-01262-8; Bayrak BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation (2025) 17:217.

designAndParticipants.sourceQuote: Our study is based on data collected from professional football players from a football team in the Turkish Super League during the 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, and 2020-2021 seasons. This was a prospective cohort study. A total of 169 players were included in the study.

definitionAndReporter.sourceQuote: Only injuries that prevented players from participating in training/match for over 72 h were recorded. These injuries were diagnosed by the club's sports physicians and/or relevant medical doctors, documented by a sports physiotherapist, and recorded immediately after the incident using a standard injury form.

severity.sourceQuote: Injuries were categorized as minimal (1-3 days of absence), minor (4-7 days of absence), moderate (8-28 days of absence), or severe/major (> 28 days of absence). The Results say 104 lasted less than 8 days and were classified as minor injuries, while 61 were moderate and 61 severe.
severity.pageHint: PDF p. 4, Methods - Injury identification; PDF p. 7, Results

incidence.sourceQuote: Over the five seasons, players experienced: 7.76 injuries per 1,000 training hours (95% CI: 7.59-7.93), 15.47 injuries per 1,000 match hours (95% CI: 15.23-15.71), 8.9 injuries per 1,000 combined training and match hours (95% CI: 8.72-9.0).

timeLossAndIllness.sourceQuote: players missed a total of 4,573 training sessions due to injuries and illnesses... 116 days missed due to illness, 550 days missed due to contact injuries, and 3,907 days missed due to non-contact injuries.

nonContact.sourceQuote: In our study, 61 of the 121 non-contact injuries (50.4%) occurred during matches, while 60 (49.6%) occurred during training.
nonContact.pageHint: PDF p. 10, Discussion - Contact vs. non-contact injury status

headlineLocation.sourceQuote: Over the five seasons, players sustained 224 injuries, with the thigh region being the most frequently injured area. The hamstring muscles were the most commonly affected anatomical structures...

locationRates.sourceQuote: The highest incidence was observed in hamstring injuries, with 2.36 injuries per 1,000 h (95% CI: 1.76-2.96). Knee injuries followed with 1.28 ... Groin ... 1.20 ... calf ... 0.88 ... both ankle and quadriceps ... 0.80...

derivations.reason: Transparent sum of direct, disjoint injury time-loss components. It is not derived from a rate.

derivations.method: Sum direct Table 4 position counts into Total, retaining each source position line.
examples: thigh Total 81 = quadriceps + hamstring + tensor fascia latae across positions; lines 6, 26, 35, 14
groin Total 33 = groin + osteitis pubis across positions; lines 0, 11, 16, 6
lower leg Total 29 = tibia + calf muscle + Achilles across positions; lines 4, 11, 11, 3
derivations.reason: These are transparent aggregations of adjacent source rows into one schema parent. They are not rate-to-count calculations.

mappingNotes.injuryLocation_groin_prevalence: Aggregates direct Table 4 Groin and Osteitis Pubis rows into the schema's groin parent.
mappingNotes.injuryLocation_thigh_prevalence: Aggregates direct Quadriceps, Hamstring and Tensor Fascia Latae rows into the schema's thigh parent.
mappingNotes.injuryLocation_lower_leg_prevalence: Aggregates direct Tibia, Calf Muscle and Achilles rows into the schema's lower-leg parent.
mappingNotes.injuryLocation_thigh_incidence: The reported 2.36 rate is hamstring-specific, stored in the available thigh parent field with its source specificity preserved here and in the Backlog note.
mappingNotes.injuryLocation_lower_leg_incidence: The reported 0.88 rate is calf-specific, stored in the available lower-leg parent field with source specificity preserved.
mappingNotes.injuryLocation_ankle_incidence: The reported 0.80 rate is directly ankle-specific. No count is staged because Table 4 gives a combined Foot-Ankle count.

participantCharacteristics: sex: the paper does not directly state participant sex; do not infer it from the league name.
meanAge: Table 2 reports injured/non-injured comparison means, not a cohort-wide mean.
injuryPlayersCompletedStudy: p. 3 both says 169 were included and describes exclusions for players who did not complete a season; no unambiguous completion total is printed.
exposure: seasonLength, totalExposure, matchExposure and trainingExposure: rates are reported, but raw exposure totals and season length are not printed. No count-to-exposure back-calculation.
injuryOutcome: injuryTotalCount: source conflict, 224 on p. 6, 229 on p. 7, and Table 4 position-row sum 227. No value is staged.
medical-attention and time-loss event counts: no separate compatible event totals are printed.
match/training total event counts: p. 10 has only non-contact match/training counts, not all-injury totals.
burden, recurrence, onset and contact-injury counts: no compatible direct values.
time-loss total uses the source's contact/non-contact components, but the paper alternates between training sessions and days; preserve the unit caveat.
illnessOutcome: Only the directly reported 116 missed units due to illness is staged. No illness count, definition, system, aetiology, incidence, burden, severity or mechanism is reported.
injuryTissueType: The source provides location/diagnosis labels rather than a clean tissue-type table. Do not force hamstring, quadriceps, calf, meniscus, ACL or chondromalacia labels into broad tissue rows without compatible counts.
injuryLocation: Vertebral column/spinal region is not mapped because the schema separates thoracic and lumbosacral and the source does not do so.
Pelvis is not mapped because it is not a clean hip field; Foot-Ankle is not mapped to separate foot or ankle count fields.
No direct overall lower-limb, upper-limb or trunk count/rate is staged; reported percentages and source categories do not establish compatible structured totals.

caveats: The primary injury count is internally inconsistent: 224 (p. 6), 229 (p. 7), and 227 when Table 4 position rows are summed. It is intentionally blank and is a reviewer-attention item.

The overall incidence is 8.9 per 1,000 combined hours in the abstract and Results (p. 1 and p. 7), but the Discussion says 8.49 (p. 9). This proposal uses the repeated abstract/Results value, preserves the 8.72-9.0 CI, and does not calculate a replacement.

The reported 4,573 and component values are described inconsistently as training sessions and days. The staged 4,457 injury time-loss value is a permitted component sum, not a claim that the source cleanly distinguishes units.
Table 4 is position-stratified and was used only for directly mappable location-count families. It should not be used to derive exposure, incidence or a reconciled overall injury count.
proposedBacklogNote: Stage A local proposal only, no extraction write. Proposed layout: Total / Goalkeeper / Defenders / Midfielders / Forwards, using Table 4 n=17/51/67/34 and directly mappable position-stratified location counts. Core surveillance is prospective over five Turkish Super League seasons. Reviewer attention: injury count conflicts (224, 229, and Table 4 sum 227); leave total injury count blank. Overall incidence is 8.9 per 1,000 combined hours in abstract/Results but 8.49 in Discussion; stage 8.9 with CI 8.72-9.0 and preserve discrepancy. Raw exposure totals are not reported. Injury time-loss total 4,457 is a permitted 550 + 3,907 component sum, but the paper alternates sessions/days. Await supported promotion and fresh additive-state check.
